review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

1:1.sourceText: Ἐπειδήπερ πολλοὶ ἐπεχείρησαν ἀνατάξασθαι διήγησιν περὶ τῶν πεπληροφορημένων ἐν ἡμῖν πραγμάτων,
1:1.targetText: Many have undertaken to compose an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,

groups.note: The attributive participle is rendered as a relative clause.

sourceMoved.reason: Ἐπειδήπερ ("since") makes 1:1-2 the reason for 1:3, where BSB states that link with Therefore.

1:2.sourceText: καθὼς παρέδοσαν ἡμῖν οἱ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς αὐτόπται καὶ ὑπηρέται γενόμενοι τοῦ λόγου,
1:2.targetText: just as they were handed down to us by the initial eyewitnesses and servants of the word.

groups.note: BSB turns the active "they delivered" into a passive with the things of 1:1 as subject.
ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, "from the beginning", is rendered by the adjective initial.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle γενόμενοι ("having become") is not separately rendered in "eyewitnesses and servants of the word".

unmappedTarget.reason: English subject of BSB's passive, referring to the things of 1:1.
English agent marker of BSB's passive; in Greek these people are the subject of the active verb.

1:3.sourceText: ἔδοξε κἀμοὶ παρηκολουθηκότι ἄνωθεν πᾶσιν ἀκριβῶς καθεξῆς σοι γράψαι, κράτιστε Θεόφιλε,
1:3.targetText: Therefore, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, it seemed good also to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,

groups.note: Ἐπειδήπερ ("since") at the head of 1:1 makes 1:1-2 the reason for 1:3; BSB states that link with Therefore here.
The adverb καθεξῆς, "in order", is rendered by the adjective orderly.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object "an account" for write; the Greek has only the adverb καθεξῆς.
English supplies the object "an account" for write; the Greek has only the adverb καθεξῆς.

1:4.sourceText: ἵνα ἐπιγνῷς περὶ ὧν κατηχήθης λόγων τὴν ἀσφάλειαν.
1:4.targetText: so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.

groups.note: The relative ὧν has drawn its noun λόγων into the clause; together they give "the things" you have been taught.

1:5.sourceText: Ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡρῴδου βασιλέως τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἱερεύς τις ὀνόματι Ζαχαρίας ἐξ ἐφημερίας Ἀβιά, καὶ γυνὴ αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων Ἀαρών, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Ἐλεισάβετ.
1:5.targetText: In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, and whose wife Elizabeth was a daughter of Aaron.

groups.note: ἐξ, "from" the division of Abijah, is rendered "belonged to".
The partitive ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων, "from the daughters", is rendered "a daughter".
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB folds "and her name was Elizabeth" into "whose wife Elizabeth", keeping only the name.

unmappedTarget.reason: Supplied relative pronoun introducing BSB's clause.
Supplied copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

1:6.sourceText: ἦσαν δὲ δίκαιοι ἀμφότεροι ἐναντίον τοῦ Θεοῦ, πορευόμενοι ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασιν τοῦ Κυρίου ἄμεμπτοι.
1:6.targetText: Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:7.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τέκνον, καθότι ἦν ἡ Ἐλεισάβετ στεῖρα, καὶ ἀμφότεροι προβεβηκότες ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῶν ἦσαν.
1:7.targetText: But they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both well along in years.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB's "well along in years" leaves "their" (days) unexpressed.

1:8.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἱερατεύειν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ τάξει τῆς ἐφημερίας αὐτοῦ ἔναντι τοῦ Θεοῦ,
1:8.targetText: One day while Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God,

groups.note: The narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ, "now it came about", is rendered "One day".
ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal "while".
ἐν τῇ τάξει, "in the turn" of his division, is rendered "on duty".
The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered by the name Zechariah.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two circumstances; the Greek has the infinitive phrase and the "in the turn" phrase without a conjunction.
Supplied copula; BSB makes the division the subject of its own clause.

1:9.sourceText: κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἱερατείας ἔλαχε τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Κυρίου,
1:9.targetText: he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι states what the lot assigned; BSB's "to" stands before "enter and burn incense".

unmappedSource.reason: εἰς is absorbed in the transitive English "enter".

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the entering participle to the infinitive with "and".

1:10.sourceText: καὶ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος ἦν τοῦ λαοῦ προσευχόμενον ἔξω τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ θυμιάματος.
1:10.targetText: And at the hour of the incense offering, the whole congregation was praying outside.

groups.note: πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ, "the multitude of the people", is rendered "congregation".

1:11.sourceText: ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἑστὼς ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ θυμιάματος.
1:11.targetText: Just then an angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered with the name Zechariah.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:12.sourceText: καὶ ἐταράχθη Ζαχαρίας ἰδών, καὶ φόβος ἐπέπεσεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν.
1:12.targetText: When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and gripped with fear.

groups.note: "Fear fell upon him" is recast with Zechariah as subject: "he was ... gripped with fear".

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.

unmappedTarget.reason: English object of saw; the Greek participle has none.

1:13.targetText: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to give him the name John.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:15.sourceText: ἔσται γὰρ μέγας ἐνώπιον Κυρίου, καὶ οἶνον καὶ σίκερα οὐ μὴ πίῃ, καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου πλησθήσεται ἔτι ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ,

1:19.targetText: “I am Gabriel,” replied the angel. “I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

1:20.targetText: And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.”
